data.body: Phase 1 confirmed with real temporary Git clones and the production drain path. A shared completed enrichment cycle was followed by independent stale-clone cycles. Before maintenance the branches merged cleanly. With both current retention paths active, merge-tree reproduced rename/rename on TICKET_DIGEST plus rename/delete and modify/delete on DONE_ENRICH. Discriminating matrix: queue deletion disabled but digest keep=1 active remained RED solely on TICKET_DIGEST; digest deletion disabled but queue prune active remained RED solely on DONE_ENRICH; both physical-deletion paths disabled became GREEN with all preexisting queue/digest paths retained and clean tracker worktrees. Later writes on the conflicted clone still returned success after three failed merge retries and grew local-ahead, matching production 867 ahead / 20063 behind. This rules out credentials, mounts, connectivity, and ordinary UUID appends. Root cause set for the observed enrichment wedge is two automatic delete_events retention paths: enrich_drain queue pruning and digest_sidecar keep=1 pruning. Clone-local claim arbitration amplifies duplicate cycles but is not sufficient to wedge an append-only store. The best-effort push policy is an intended amplifier and will not be changed. A separate discovered bug, 55bc-b6bf-7adc-4108, tracks the same destructive-retention pattern in plan-review, code-review, and completion sidecars; those siblings require their own real two-clone RED proof before repair.
